'Establishment' is defined here but its recordkeeping consequences live in establishments.json alongside 1904.30.

physician_or_other_licensed_health_care_.term: Physician or Other Licensed Health Care Professional (PLHCP)
physician_or_other_licensed_health_care_.definition: An individual whose legally permitted scope of practice — their license, registration or certification — allows them to independently perform, or to be delegated the responsibility to perform, the activities described by Part 1904.
physician_or_other_licensed_health_care_.note: The test is what the person's licence permits, not what they are called. A nurse practitioner, audiologist or physical therapist may be a PLHCP for the activity in question; someone acting outside their permitted scope is not, whatever their title.

injury_or_illness.definition: An abnormal condition or disorder. Injuries include cases such as a cut, fracture, sprain or amputation. Illnesses include both acute and chronic conditions such as a skin disease, respiratory disorder or poisoning.
injury_or_illness.note: The lists are illustrative, not exhaustive. An injury or illness is recordable only if it is a new, work-related case meeting one or more of the Part 1904 recording criteria — the definition itself decides nothing.

establishment.definition: A single physical location where business is conducted or where services or industrial operations are performed. For operations without a single physical location — construction, transportation, communications, electric, gas and sanitary services and similar — the establishment is the main or branch office, terminal or station that supervises the activity or is the base from which personnel carry it out.
establishment.note: See establishments.json for the 1904.46(1)-(3) boundary tests and the 1904.30 recordkeeping consequences.

the_act.definition: The Occupational Safety and Health Act of 1970 (29 U.S.C. 651 et seq.). The definitions in section 3 of the Act (29 U.S.C. 652) and related interpretations apply to those terms when used in Part 1904.

you.definition: An employer as defined in section 3 of the Occupational Safety and Health Act of 1970 (29 U.S.C. 652).
